title: Bootstrap by game: the market's MLB calibration is statistically perfect
headline_insight: Resampling whole games 1000 times, 0 of 10 MLB market probability bins deviate from the diagonal beyond noise, while the model misses in 4 of 10 -- worst at the top, where 0.9541-favorites win just 0.6632 (gap -0.2909).
what_it_means: A cluster bootstrap (resampling game_id, 1000 draws) asks which calibration gaps survive sampling noise. For the market, none do -- its in-game MLB prices are indistinguishable from perfectly calibrated. The model has four real misses, the largest being overconfidence on near-locks: the 0.9-1.0 bin predicts 0.9541 but wins only 0.6632.
how_to_read: Each bin shows a gap (predicted minus actual) with a 95% confidence interval; if the interval excludes 0, the miss is real rather than noise.
why_it_matters: It separates genuine model weaknesses from statistical mirages, so improvement effort goes only to gaps that will still be there next month.
caveat: Soccer is much noisier -- 8 of 10 model bins and even 6 of 10 market bins deviate significantly on just 51 games, so the small corpus limits any firm conclusion there.
